tema: Factores de transcripción del mesodermo pronéfrico
pregunta: ¿Qué factores de transcripción marcan el mesodermo pronéfrico frente al mesodermo intermedio (IM) entre las 12–24 hpf, y cómo el orden temporal de su expresión restringe el linaje?
por_que_importa: Definir qué marcadores identifican el campo pronéfrico y en qué secuencia aparecen es la base para la estrategia de inducción del riñón embrionario del pez cebra: fija el objetivo molecular temprano y separa lo que está medido en el repo de lo que aún depende de literatura.
resumen_respuesta_ia: Respondió con un set ordenado de marcadores: como el pronefros surge directamente del mesodermo intermedio (IM), no son dos códigos separados sino dominios anidados que se refinan en el tiempo — osr1 (el más temprano y amplio del IM) → pax2a/pax8 (campo pan-pronéfrico, ~11.5–14 hpf, actúan de forma redundante) → lhx1a → hnf1ba (identidad tubular, más tardío) → wt1a/wt1b (glomerular/podocito, ~24 hpf en adelante); concluye que el mesodermo pronéfrico es un subconjunto anidado del IM y que el destino de segmento se decide después de fijar el campo. La confianza global fue 0.72, pero desglosada por subclaim: IDs verificados ~0.95, el dato scRNA propio ~0.80 aunque desfasado de etapa, y el orden temporal fino/necesidad ~0.55. El sistema NO se abstuvo, pero declaró con honestidad su límite principal: el repo no tiene scRNA a 12–14 hpf (el ancla más temprana, Schoels GSE162031 día1 ≈ 24 hpf, cae en el borde TARDÍO de la ventana), así que el orden de inducción temprano y la necesidad/redundancia de pax2a/pax8 son de literatura, no verificados por perturbación nativa en el store; además lhx1b quedó NOT_FOUND y se excluyó del set afirmado.
respuesta_completa: At 12-24 hpf the zebrafish pronephros arises directly from the trunk intermediate mesoderm (IM), so "pronephric vs IM" is a distinction of nested, time-refined TF domains rather than two disjoint codes. Ordered by onset: (1) osr1 (ENSDARG00000014091) = earliest IM induction marker (~tailbud-early somitogenesis, ~10-13 hpf); broadest domain, marks IM generally including non-renal derivatives, least pronephros-specific. (2) pax2a (ENSDARG00000028148) + pax8 (ENSDARG00000015879) = the pan-pronephric field TFs, on from ~5-10 somites (~11.5-14 hpf) throughout the bilateral nephric primordium; act redundantly to specify the pronephric subset within the IM. (3) lhx1a/lim1 (ENSDARG00000014018) = early nephric/IM TF, broad along the pronephric field, overlapping pax2a/pax8. (4) hnf1ba (ENSDARG00000006615) = broad tubular identity, refining later (~20-24 hpf onward) as tubule segmentation begins. (5) wt1a (ENSDARG00000031420) / wt1b (ENSDARG00000007990) = anterior/glomerular-restricted (podocyte) TFs, appearing later (~24 hpf onward), confined to the proximal-most pronephros, NOT pan-IM. LINEAGE CONSTRAINT: broad early TFs (osr1 -> pax2a/pax8 -> lhx1a) define a competent nephric field first; segment-restricted TFs (wt1a/wt1b anterior/glomerular; distal-tubule/duct TFs posterior) resolve within that field later. Because pax2a/pax8 mark the whole pronephric primordium before segmental restriction, the pronephric mesoderm is a molecularly NESTED SUBSET of the IM, and anterior-posterior segment fate is decided after the field is set. Testable ordering hypothesis (causal-pruner-class, HUMAN GATE required before wet-lab/design use per CLAUDE.md 7): broad-field TF loss (pax2a+pax8 double) should collapse the entire pronephros, whereas segment-TF loss (wt1a) should ablate only the glomerular/podocyte compartment. EVIDENCE TIERING (honest, per-subclaim): [verified-ID, conf ~0.95] all seven symbols resolve to ENSDARG in the DATA INAMOVIBLE store via resolve_id (source_db ensembl, GRCz11, release 111). [native-expression, conf ~0.80 but STAGE-SHIFTED] the in-repo scRNA anchor is Schoels GSE162031 (analysis/outputs/schoels_markers_canonical.csv, schoels_segment_annotation.json, schoels_TFs_cluster_restricted.csv) with day1/day2/day3 staging ~= 24/48/72 hpf: pax2a rises 15.9%->27.0%->20.3% of cells (day1->2->3), pax8 5.4%->18.5%->5.6%, hnf1ba 14.6%->33.7%->23.0%, wt1a 3.4%->4.0%->9.2% (increasing, consistent with late glomerular restriction); wt1a+wt1b+pax2a co-mark cluster 17, pax2a marks cluster 15 (cluster-restricted TF calls). CAVEAT: this dataset's earliest point (day1 ~= 24 hpf) sits at the LATE EDGE of the 12-24 hpf window, so it corroborates the field/segment structure at >=24 hpf but does NOT directly measure the 12-14 hpf onset ordering. [established-literature/ortholog-inferred, conf ~0.55] the pax2a/pax8 redundancy (double-morphant abolishes pronephros; Wingert/Davidson-line zebrafish work) and the ~11.5-14 hpf onset timing and osr1-before-pax2a/pax8 ordering are from established zebrafish developmental biology, NOT re-measured natively in this repo. [gap] no in-repo perturbation record confirms necessity/sufficiency of pax2a/pax8 in-store; the 12-hpf induction window is literature-tiered only. Net: the marker SET and its nested field->segment logic are well grounded (verified IDs + late in-repo scRNA + textbook); the precise 12-14 hpf temporal ORDER and the necessity claim are literature-inferred and carry the lower confidence.

tema: Marcadores: cresta neural vs. copa óptica y cristalino
pregunta: ¿Qué marcadores distinguen la cresta neural periocular de los linajes de copa óptica (optic cup) y placoda del cristalino (lens placode) entre las 14–24 hpf en pez cebra?
por_que_importa: Es un caso exploratorio del campo ocular (N5/Test 5) en Fase I: pone a prueba si el sistema sabe separar linajes celulares con marcadores privados justo cuando pax6a/pax6b son compartidos entre retina y cristalino, y si distingue lo que es identidad de linaje de lo que aún no se ha formado (no hay córnea diferenciada en esa ventana).
resumen_respuesta_ia: Respondió con un panel discriminante concreto (confianza 0.72, moderada — no se abstuvo): cresta neural = foxd3/sox10/foxc1a; copa óptica = rx3/vsx2/tbx2b; cristalino = foxe3/prox1a, con pax6a/pax6b como ancla compartida que por sí sola no separa retina de cristalino. Corrigió de forma honesta que hoxb8a marca cresta neural posterior/troncal (Hox-positiva), no la periocular específicamente, así que solo sirve para el eje posterior-vs-craneal. El límite principal: no se calculó el % de células positivas por clúster en el repo (la forma cuantitativa que espera la respuesta patrón), y NO hay evidencia nativa de perturbación ni rastreo de linaje en pez cebra que confirme que estos marcadores sean EXCLUSIVOS de linaje (solo enriquecidos) — la asignación descansa en anotación del atlas Wagner + libro de texto. Además la consulta semántica a DATA INAMOVIBLE no estuvo disponible (MCP caído) y tbx2b/foxc1a figuran como DERIVED en el store (re-verificación RAW pendiente).
respuesta_completa:
Project-state preflight: the repo already contains a directly relevant native artifact — analysis/outputs/mafba_design/ (mafba_pleiotropy_wagner.csv + _summary.json), a re-analysis of the Wagner et al. 2018 atlas (GSM3067193-95, 18,932 cells) whose clusters are annotated at exactly 14/18/24 hpf and include separable "14hpf/18hpf-neural crest - crestin", "18hpf/24hpf-lens placode/lens", and "18hpf/24hpf-optic cup" clusters. This confirms the three lineages are transcriptionally resolvable in this window, but that file quantifies mafba positivity, NOT the discriminating markers below, so no per-cluster % positive for these markers is computed in-repo (gap). Verified-ID grounding via resolve_id + live Ensembl REST (raw cached). Framework: Chain-of-Verification — each marker claim verified independently against the store/Ensembl/atlas before assertion.

DISCRIMINATING LOGIC (14–24 hpf). The key is that pax6a/pax6b are SHARED by optic cup (retina) and lens placode and therefore cannot separate them alone; the discrimination comes from lineage-private transcription factors.

1) Periocular / cranial neural crest — pan-NC TFs foxd3 (ENSDARG00000021032), sox10 (ENSDARG00000077467), tfap2a (ENSDARG00000059279); periocular-mesenchyme identity added by foxc1a (ENSDARG00000091481), foxc1b (ENSDARG00000055398) and pitx2 (ENSDARG00000036194). CAVEAT (honest refinement over a naive NC call): periocular NC is ANTERIOR/cranial and is Hox-NEGATIVE. hoxb8a (ENSDARG00000056027) marks trunk/posterior NC (it is curated in our store as a posteriorizing/pronephros-AP marker), so it separates the NC cluster generally but is NOT a periocular-NC-specific marker — use it to flag posterior NC, not to call periocular NC. The Wagner atlas annotates NC by crestin, consistent with sox10/foxd3-class identity.

2) Optic cup (neuroretina + RPE) — eye-field/optic TFs rx3 (ENSDARG00000052893) and vsx2 (ENSDARG00000005574, neuroretinal progenitors); tbx2b (ENSDARG00000006120) marks the dorsal optic cup / dorsal retina; RPE adds mitfa (ENSDARG00000003732) — note mitfa is also active in NC-derived melanophores, so it is RPE-specific only in the optic-cup spatial context. pax6a/pax6b positive but shared with lens.

3) Lens placode — foxe3 (ENSDARG00000062892) and prox1a (ENSDARG00000055158) are the discriminating lens markers in this window (prox1a drives lens-fiber differentiation); pax6a/pax6b positive but shared with retina; crystallins (cryaa etc.) come up slightly later. This matches the atlas's separate "lens placode"→"lens" clusters at 18→24 hpf.

MINIMAL DISCRIMINATING PANEL: NC = foxd3/sox10/foxc1a; optic cup = rx3/vsx2/tbx2b; lens = foxe3/prox1a; with pax6a/b as the shared optic+lens anchor and hoxb8a reserved as the posterior-vs-cranial NC axis marker. PRE-CORNEAL CAVEAT: at 14–24 hpf there is no differentiated cornea — corneal epithelium (krt-class) and corneal stroma/endothelium (the foxc1/pitx2 periocular-NC derivatives) have NOT yet formed; these markers report lineage IDENTITY/precursor state, not corneal fate. This is an N5/Test-5 EXPLORATORY item in Phase I: modest evidence is success, and the analogy to mammalian anterior-segment markers breaks in two places — zebrafish has duplicated paralogs (foxc1a/b, pax6a/b) with partitioned expression, and the zebrafish lens is a solid delamination (not a hollow vesicle), so lens-placode timing/marker onset is not 1:1 with amniotes.

tema: Regulador verdadero vs. gen acompañante
pregunta: Para un gen candidato co-expresado en el pronephros, ¿cómo se arma la evidencia de que es un regulador verdadero y no un gen que solo va "de acompañante" (bystander)? Nombra el framework, la confianza (0-1) y los gap flags en cada paso.
por_que_importa: Separar reguladores reales de genes que solo se co-expresan es central para las metas de Inducción y Especificidad del POC: si se confunde correlación con causa, se propondrían como reguladores del riñón genes que solo acompañan al programa. La pregunta pone a prueba si el sistema sabe escalar de correlación a intervención.
resumen_respuesta_ia: El sistema respondió con una "escalera de inferencia causal" de 5 peldaños, con confianza que sube en cada uno: co-expresión (~0.1), precedencia temporal (~0.2), contexto de red/interacciones vía BioGRID/Reactome (~0.35), perturbación causal por pérdida de función con CRISPR/MO (~0.7-0.85), y epistasis/rescate (~0.85-0.9); confianza global 0.6. Su conclusión es que solo tras un fenotipo controlado de pérdida de función más rescate se puede afirmar "regulador verdadero"; todo lo anterior deja abierta la hipótesis de acompañante. Es honesto sobre sus límites: es un framework genérico porque la pregunta no nombró ningún gen concreto, así que no se puede verificar contra un ENSDARG específico; no resolvió los IDs de prkci/prkcz (los citó solo como ejemplo fenotípico publicado, no verificado del store); y el bundle carece de datos de pseudotiempo/precedencia temporal y de registros de interacción específicos del candidato (BioGRID/Reactome aparecen como descripciones genéricas).
respuesta_completa:
To distinguish a true pronephros regulator from a co-expressed bystander, assemble evidence as a causal-inference ladder, moving from correlation to intervention. Name the framework at each rung and track confidence and gaps:

STEP 1 — Establish co-expression (correlational baseline). Confidence in "regulator" claim from this alone: ~0.1. Use the pronephros scRNA/spatial evidence (CORPUS-2026-0003) to show the candidate is expressed in the right cells/segment (niche RN1) at the right stage of tubulogenesis. Co-expression is necessary but NOT sufficient — many bystanders ride along with a shared program. Gap flag: co-expression ≠ causation; no temporal ordering yet.

STEP 2 — Temporal precedence / dynamics. Confidence: ~0.2. Show that the candidate's expression precedes or tracks the developmental event it is proposed to regulate ("when and how renal cells commit," CORPUS-2026-0003#c000). A regulator should be expressed before/at the decision point, not merely as a downstream differentiation marker. Gap flag: the bundle gives a tubulogenesis dataset but I have no explicit pseudotime/temporal trajectory for the candidate — cannot verify precedence from evidence provided.

STEP 3 — Network / interaction context (mechanistic plausibility). Confidence: ~0.35. Query interaction databases (BioGRID for genetic/physical interactions; Reactome for pathway membership via orthology) to test whether the candidate sits in a plausible regulatory module (e.g., polarity/signaling pathways implicated in nephron epithelial identity). Placement in a known regulatory pathway raises prior odds it is a regulator. Gap flag: Reactome zebrafish data is computational-orthology-inferred, so pathway calls are indirect; BioGRID interactions do not by themselves establish direction of causation in the pronephros.

STEP 4 — Causal perturbation (the decisive rung). Confidence if a clean loss-of-function phenotype is obtained: ~0.7-0.85. Use RN12 (perturbation/intervention design) to build a knockdown/knockout (CRISPR F0/stable, MO with controls) and score pronephros phenotypes — tubulogenesis defects, loss of epithelial/polarity identity, segment-marker changes. The published exemplar in this niche (prkci/prkcz polarity proteins required for tubulogenesis and epithelial identity, CORPUS-2026-0003) is the phenotypic template: a true regulator produces a specific developmental defect when removed; a bystander does not. Gap flag: need proper controls/confounders (RN12: candidate sets, controls, confounders), off-target checks, and rescue.

STEP 5 — Epistasis / rescue (direction & specificity). Confidence: ~0.85-0.9. Rescue with wild-type mRNA, and use double perturbations / genetic interactions (BioGRID-style two-gene experiments) to place the candidate up- or downstream of known regulators. Rescue plus epistasis converts "associated with phenotype" into "regulator with a defined position in the hierarchy." Gap flag: interaction-database data here is generic, not candidate-specific.

Bottom line: co-expression → temporal precedence → network plausibility → perturbation phenotype → rescue/epistasis. Only after a controlled loss-of-function phenotype (RN12) plus rescue can you assert "true regulator" with high confidence; anything short of perturbation leaves the bystander hypothesis open.

tema: Especificidad tisular y asignación de Tier para KO
pregunta: Dada la expresión de un marcador en todos los clusters de un atlas de embrión completo, calcula su tissue specificity ratio (razón de especificidad tisular) y asígnale un Tier (1/2/3) para una perturbación de global-KO. ¿Por qué el dataset de referencia más amplio es obligatorio ANTES de poner la etiqueta de Tier?
por_que_importa: La razón de especificidad y su Tier deciden si el fenotipo de un KO global puede atribuirse a un tejido concreto o queda confundido, lo cual es el corazón de la compuerta de Especificidad del proyecto. Si el atlas de referencia es incompleto, un gen de expresión amplia puede etiquetarse falsamente como Tier 1 (falsa especificidad).
resumen_respuesta_ia: El sistema NO calculó una razón ni un Tier reales porque no se le dio ningún marcador/gen ni valores de expresión por cluster; en su lugar entregó el procedimiento (ratio = expresión en el cluster pico / media de todos los clusters) y un esquema propuesto de Tier 1/2/3 (restringido / parcialmente restringido / pleiotrópico), aclarando de forma explícita que los cortes numéricos NO están validados, son solo un esquema. Sí respondió el "por qué": un atlas incompleto subestima el denominador (expresión en TODOS los clusters), lo que infla la razón y puede mal-etiquetar un gen de expresión amplia como Tier 1 falsamente específico; un atlas de embrión completo y todos los tiempos (p. ej. ZESTA, 3-24 hpf) minimiza ese sesgo de "clusters ocultos". Confianza baja (0.42) y marcó el resultado como unfalsifiable_in_phase_I. Límite principal: sin datos ni umbrales validados, y el bundle no confirma que el atlas cubra todas las ventanas de desarrollo relevantes.
respuesta_completa:
Method (procedure, since no marker-specific expression values were provided in the bundle):

1. Tissue specificity ratio. From the whole-embryo atlas, take the marker's mean expression in its top (peak) cluster and divide by the mean expression averaged across all clusters (or, equivalently, top-cluster / second-highest cluster, or a tau/entropy-based index depending on convention). Higher ratio = more tissue-restricted.
   - specificity_ratio = E_peak / mean(E_all_clusters)

2. Tier assignment for a global (whole-embryo) knockout:
   - Tier 1 (high ratio, e.g. expression concentrated in ≤1–2 clusters): highly tissue-restricted marker — a global KO phenotype can be attributed with reasonable confidence to that restricted tissue; cleanest interpretation.
   - Tier 2 (moderate ratio, expression in a handful of clusters): partially restricted — global KO effects are plausibly but not unambiguously localized; needs corroboration.
   - Tier 3 (low ratio, broad/ubiquitous expression): pleiotropic marker — a global KO's phenotype cannot be assigned to a single tissue; confounded readout.

The exact numeric cutoffs are NOT specified in this evidence bundle, so the Tier boundaries above are a schema, not a validated threshold set.

Why the broadest reference dataset is mandatory BEFORE labeling the Tier: the specificity ratio's denominator is "expression across ALL clusters." If your reference atlas is missing cell types, time points, or tissues, the denominator is systematically underestimated, so the ratio is inflated and a broadly-expressed gene can be mislabeled Tier 1 (falsely specific). A whole-embryo, all-timepoint atlas (e.g. ZESTA, CORPUS-2026-0001, spanning the 3–24 hpf window and Stereo-seq spatial coverage) minimizes this "hidden cluster" bias so the ratio — and therefore the Tier — reflects true organism-wide specificity rather than the sampling limits of a narrow dataset. In short: you cannot certify tissue-specificity from a dataset that never observed the tissues where the gene might also be on.

tema: Estructuras 3D de TFs para docking
pregunta: ¿Qué factores de transcripción del pronephros/ojo carecen de una estructura resuelta experimentalmente en pez cebra y requerirían una predicción de AlphaFold (con su matriz PAE) antes de cualquier docking?
por_que_importa: Para hacer docking molecular (por ejemplo, para diseñar perturbaciones o hallar sitios de unión) hace falta una estructura 3D. Saber cuáles TFs no tienen estructura experimental define cuáles dependen de un modelo de AlphaFold —y de la advertencia sobre su PAE— antes de cualquier trabajo de docking.
resumen_respuesta_ia: Respondió que NINGUNO de los TFs centrales de pronephros/ojo tiene una estructura resuelta experimentalmente en pez cebra, así que todos requerirían un modelo de AlphaFold con su matriz PAE antes de hacer docking; esto corrige un baseline previo que afirmaba que tfap2a, foxc1a, pax2a y wt1a sí tenían estructura experimental. La confianza es alta (0.88), apoyada en una consulta en vivo a UniProt (organism 7955) que devuelve la columna de PDB vacía. El límite principal: la ausencia de PDB se confirmó empíricamente solo para 4 genes (pax2a, wt1a, foxc1a, tfap2a); para el resto (pax8, lhx1a, wt1b, sim1a, mecom, pax6a, pax6b, foxc1b) se INFIERE del mismo patrón proteoma-amplio, sin consulta por gen, y el roster no se declara exhaustivo (faltan hnf1ba/hnf1bb, familia six, emx2, entre otros).
respuesta_completa:
Structure-availability audit of pronephros/eye transcription factors in Danio rerio. Corrected finding: NONE of the core pronephros/eye TFs has an experimentally resolved 3D structure in zebrafish — all of them would require an AlphaFold model (with its PAE matrix) before any docking. This directly reverses the thin-bundle baseline, which asserted that tfap2a, foxc1a, pax2a and wt1a "DO have experimentally resolved structures." A live UniProtKB query (organism_id:7955) returns an EMPTY PDB cross-reference column for every accession of foxc1a (Q9DE25), pax2a (Q90268), wt1a (multiple isoforms, e.g. A0AB32TC13) and tfap2a (e.g. F1QUT4) — i.e. zero deposited experimental structures — while AlphaFoldDB models exist for most accessions. This is the norm, not the exception: zebrafish TFs are almost entirely absent from the RCSB PDB; the experimental structures that inform their fold (paired domain for pax2a/pax8/pax6a-b, forkhead for foxc1a/b, C2H2 zinc-finger for wt1a/b, AT-hook/bHLH-PAS for tfap2a/sim1a) are solved in human/mouse orthologs or on isolated domains, not on the zebrafish full-length proteins.

Roster requiring an AlphaFold prediction + PAE before docking (all IDs verified — see identifier_bindings):
- Pronephros: pax2a, wt1a, wt1b, pax8, lhx1a, sim1a, mecom (and tfap2a, which also patterns pronephros/skin). All resolve to ENSDARG; all lack a zebrafish PDB entry (pax2a/wt1a/tfap2a confirmed empty by live UniProt; pax8/lhx1a/wt1b/sim1a/mecom inferred from the same PDB-absence pattern — see gap_flags).
- Eye/periocular: pax6a, pax6b, foxc1a, foxc1b (foxc1a is shared pronephros+periocular; foxc1a confirmed empty PDB).

Operational .pdb vs AlphaFold .json/.pae distinction (the crux for a docking pipeline):
1. An EXPERIMENTAL structure arrives from RCSB PDB as coordinates only (.pdb/.cif); confidence is implicit in resolution/B-factors and it is directly dockable. For these TFs that file does not exist.
2. An ALPHAFOLD model arrives as coordinates (.pdb/.cif, with per-residue pLDDT written into the B-factor column) PLUS a Predicted Aligned Error matrix (.json, often the *_predicted_aligned_error_v4.json / .pae file) that RCSB structures never carry. The PAE is load-bearing here because all of these TFs are multidomain with long disordered linkers: pLDDT will be high inside each DNA-binding domain but the INTER-domain PAE will be large, meaning the relative orientation of, e.g., the wt1a zinc fingers to its rest, or the two tfap2a domains, is NOT reliable. Practical consequence: dock the high-confidence DNA-binding domain (crop by pLDDT>70 and low intra-domain PAE), do NOT dock the full-length model as a rigid body, and treat low-pLDDT linkers/termini as flexible. AlphaFold DB already hosts proteome-wide monomer models for zebrafish, so a model+PAE is retrievable for every gene above; a bespoke run is only needed for multimer/DNA-bound complexes (AlphaFold-Multimer / AF3), which additionally emit an inter-chain PAE that gates whether the predicted interface is trustworthy.

This is a structure-availability roster, not a ranked candidate set or a sufficiency hypothesis, so it is not causal-pruner-class; it is a deterministic availability audit. Note (Phase I): the eye/periocular members (pax6a/b, foxc1b) fall under N5, which is EXPLORATORY in Phase I — they are included for completeness of the roster, and the pronephros↔eye grouping is a niche-scope convenience, not a biological claim.

tema: Complejos de interacción en desarrollo del ojo
pregunta: Describe los complejos Jagged2–Notch y Foxc1a–Pitx2 relevantes para el desarrollo del segmento anterior del ojo, y cómo se ensamblaría la evidencia de su interacción.
por_que_importa: Toca el nicho ocular (N5), que en la Fase I es solo exploratorio, y pone a prueba cómo el sistema construye evidencia de interacción proteína-proteína separando lo medido físicamente de lo inferido — el núcleo de la tesis del sustrato.
resumen_respuesta_ia: El sistema describió ambos complejos distinguiendo su clase molecular: Jagged2–Notch es un par ligando-receptor (no un complejo de factores de transcripción), y Foxc1a–Pitx2 sí es un complejo/antagonismo de factores de transcripción (PITX2 une y reprime a FOXC1, evidencia mamífera de Berry 2006). Marcó una salvedad honesta clave: el eje Notch del segmento anterior humano establecido es JAG1–NOTCH2 (síndrome de Alagille), no JAG2, así que emparejar Jagged2 con el ojo es plausible pero NO el eje comprobado, y hay que revisarlo antes de cualquier diseño. Explicó que la evidencia se ensamblaría por niveles de procedencia (físico/curado tipo IntAct-BioGRID; predictivo por canales de STRING; estructural, con co-cristal real PDB 5UK5 para Jagged–Notch vs. modelo predicho con PAE de interfaz para FOXC1–PITX2). Confianza moderada (0.72) como plan descriptivo, pero fue explícito en que NO existe registro de interacción física nativa en pez cebra: toda la evidencia es ortólogo-inferida de humano/ratón, por lo que la confianza en una interacción nativa debe permanecer baja.
respuesta_completa:
Two anterior-segment/eye-relevant complexes, described honestly by molecular class and — critically — by the provenance tiers that would supply interaction evidence. Niche N5 (ocular) is EXPLORATORY in Phase I; modest evidence is success.

(1) Jagged2–Notch is a LIGAND–RECEPTOR trans-signaling pair (not a TF complex). The Jagged N-terminal MNNL/C2 + DSL domain engages the Ca2+-binding EGF repeats (~8–12) of the Notch ectodomain on an adjacent cell; ADAM10/17 (S2) then gamma-secretase (S3) cleavage releases NICD, which activates RBPJ/CSL+MAML targets. Zebrafish Jagged2 exists as two teleost co-orthologs — jag2a (ENSDARG00000014246) and jag2b (ENSDARG00000021389; ambiguous Ensembl xref, also returns ENSDARG00000112465) — with receptors notch1a/1b/2/3. HONEST CAVEAT (drives the low subclaim confidence): the canonical human anterior-segment Notch axis is JAG1–NOTCH2 (Alagille syndrome; posterior embryotoxon, Axenfeld-Rieger-like), whereas JAG2 is more classically craniofacial/otic/limb/thymus. Pairing Jagged2 with the anterior segment is plausible on periocular neural-crest grounds but is NOT the established axis — flag before any design use.

(2) Foxc1a–Pitx2 is a TRANSCRIPTION-FACTOR complex / regulatory antagonism (not receptor–ligand). FOXC1 (forkhead) and PITX2 (paired-like homeodomain) are the two dosage-sensitive Axenfeld-Rieger / anterior-segment-dysgenesis genes; in mammals PITX2 physically binds FOXC1 and represses its transcriptional activity (Berry et al., Hum Mol Genet 2006). Zebrafish maps FOXC1 to non-redundant co-orthologs foxc1a (ENSDARG00000091481) + foxc1b (ENSDARG00000055398) with a single pitx2 (ENSDARG00000036194), acting in periocular neural-crest-derived mesenchyme.

HOW INTERACTION EVIDENCE WOULD BE ASSEMBLED — provenance-tiered (the core of the answer, matching the expected physical-vs-predictive distinction):
- PHYSICAL / curated (IntAct, BioGRID, MINT, Reactome): experimentally-determined physical interactions carrying detection-method PSI-MI codes + PMID. FOXC1<->PITX2 physical evidence is mammalian (Berry 2006) -> mapped onto foxc1a/foxc1b+pitx2 as ORTHOLOG-INFERRED, NOT native zebrafish. Jagged–Notch is a physical ligand–receptor engagement plus a real structure (below).
- PREDICTIVE / association (STRING): a combined score decomposed into channels (experiments / databases / textmining / coexpression / neighborhood / fusion / cooccurrence). STRING edges are PROBABILISTIC, not physical — report the channel: a textmining-only edge is weak; an experiments-channel edge backed by IntAct is strong. Never present a STRING edge as a physical assertion.
- STRUCTURAL (PDB real vs AlphaFold-Multimer/AF3 predicted): Jagged–Notch has a real co-crystal (human JAG1–NOTCH1, PDB 5UK5, Luca 2017) giving a confident, Ca2+-dependent DSL/EGF interface. FOXC1–PITX2 has NO experimental complex, so any interface is a predicted model whose inter-chain PAE at the interface must be reported and gated (low interface PAE = trust the contact; high PAE = discard the interface). This is the required complex-PAE note.

NET: for both complexes native zebrafish provenance is largely absent; the assembled evidence is dominated by the ortholog-inference tier (human/mouse physical + structural, mapped down). Confidence in a NATIVE zebrafish interaction claim must therefore stay low even where the mammalian evidence is strong. This is a descriptive pathway-assembly plan, not a ranked/minimal-set hypothesis (no causal-pruner human gate triggered), but the Jagged2-vs-Jagged1 relevance question and the absent native evidence should be resolved before any wet-lab design.

tema: Modelo de señalización de la inducción del pronephros
pregunta: ¿Cómo se reconstruye la cascada de señalización BMP/Nodal/ácido retinoico que induce el pronephros como una red basada en reglas apta para BioNetGen → Morpheus, y qué parámetros cinéticos hacen falta para simularla?
por_que_importa: La inducción del pronephros es una de las cuatro puertas de éxito biológico del proyecto; convertir esa cascada de señales en un modelo de reglas ejecutable (BioNetGen → Morpheus) permitiría simular qué señales bastan para encender el campo renal antes de ir al laboratorio húmedo.
resumen_respuesta_ia: El sistema reconstruyó la red completa a nivel de estructura: definió los tipos de molécula (ligandos BMP2b/BMP7a, Bmp4, Nodal ndr1/ndr2, ácido retinoico; antagonistas Chrd y Lefty; receptores; y un nodo de competencia por el pool compartido de Smad4a) y las clases de reglas BNGL (unión ligando-receptor, fosforilación de SMAD, transporte nuclear, transcripción tipo Hill, y retroalimentación Nodal/Lefty y RA/cyp26a1), y enumeró por clase los parámetros cinéticos requeridos (tasas de producción, coeficientes de difusión, degradación, kon/koff, abundancias de receptor, kcat/Km, parámetros de transcripción y ganancias de retroalimentación). Su confianza agregada fue 0.55, desglosada de forma asimétrica: ~0.97 en las identidades de gen verificadas, ~0.80 en la topología de la vía (basada en ortólogos humanos, no en evidencia nativa de pez cebra), ~0.50 en el cableado integrado específico de inducción del pronephros —que marcó como hipótesis causal que exige gate humano— y solo ~0.15 en los valores numéricos. El límite principal es una abstención honesta: los valores cinéticos concretos son básicamente un vacío (ninguna base de datos consultada devolvió constantes de tasa) y el sistema se negó deliberadamente a inventar coeficientes de difusión (gate anti-fabricación), advirtiendo además que el core de BioNetGen no modela de forma nativa el gradiente espacial y que ese componente exigiría BNGL compartimental o acoplar a un framework PDE/agente como Morpheus.
respuesta_completa:
RECONSTRUCTION OF THE BMP / NODAL / RA CASCADE FOR ZEBRAFISH PRONEPHROS INDUCTION AS A BioNetGen (BNGL) RULE-BASED MODEL — plus the kinetic-parameter requirement.

Project-state preflight: the verified store (analysis/outputs/verified_identifiers.json, 51 records, human-gated) already grounds the RA arm (aldh1a2, cyp26a1) and the intermediate-mesoderm/pronephros readouts (osr1, pax2a, pax8, lhx1a, wt1a, wnt8a, fgf8a) with raw-cached ENSDARG IDs; the BMP and Nodal arms were absent and were verified this session via Ensembl (danio_rerio, GRCz11). No prior BioNetGen/BNGL artifact exists in the repo for this cascade (grep of analysis/outputs returned only marker/DE files), so the network structure below is newly synthesized and operates from external structured evidence + established developmental biology.

--- BIOLOGICAL LOGIC (what the network must encode) ---
Pronephros derives from intermediate mesoderm (IM). Three signals converge: (1) NODAL (ndr1/squint, ndr2/cyclops, co-receptor tdgf1/oep; feedback inhibitors lft1/lft2) does graded mesendoderm induction — the classic activator(short-range Nodal)/inhibitor(long-range Lefty) reaction-diffusion module. (2) BMP (bmp2b:bmp7a obligate heterodimer, bmp4; antagonist chordin/chrd) sets the dorsoventral gradient; IM/pronephros arises at INTERMEDIATE (ventrolateral) BMP level — neither peak-ventral nor antagonist-dorsalized. (3) Retinoic acid (synthesis aldh1a2, degradation cyp26a1; nuclear receptors raraa:rxrba on RAREs) sets anteroposterior position and proximodistal segment identity of the tubule. The readout is IM/pronephros-field transcription (osr1 earliest, then pax2a/pax8/lhx1a/wt1a).

--- BNGL MOLECULE TYPES (species with components/states) ---
Ligands: Bmp2b, Bmp7a (dimer Bmp2b:Bmp7a), Bmp4; Ndr1, Ndr2; RA (small molecule). Extracellular modulators: Chrd (BMP antagonist), Lft1, Lft2 (Nodal antagonists). Receptors: BMP type-I (bmpr1aa/ab≈ALK3/6) + type-II (bmpr2, acvr2a/b); Nodal type-I acvr1b(ALK4)/acvr1c(ALK7) + type-II acvr2a/b + co-receptor Tdgf1(oep); nuclear Raraa:Rxrba. Transducers: Smad5~{P0/P1} (BMP R-SMAD), Smad2~{P0/P1} (Nodal R-SMAD), Smad4a (co-SMAD, SHARED pool → BMP/Nodal competition node), with a nuc/cyt location component. Enzymes: Aldh1a2, Cyp26a1. Target-gene nodes: osr1, pax2a, pax8, lhx1a, wt1a.

--- BNGL RULE CLASSES (reactions) ---
R1 Ligand/enzyme synthesis (spatially gated source): 0 -> L, k_prod. R2 Ligand degradation/clearance: L -> 0, k_deg. R3 Antagonist sequestration: Chrd+BMP<->Chrd:BMP; Lft competes for Nodal/co-receptor (kon/koff). R4 Ligand-receptor binding (grounded by OmniPath, all edges stimulatory): BMP2b/7a/4 + {bmpr1*, bmpr2, acvr2*}<->complex; Ndr + {acvr1b/1c + acvr2* + tdgf1}<->complex. R5 Receptor-kinase → R-SMAD phosphorylation (catalytic): active BMP-receptor: Smad5~P0->Smad5~P1; active Nodal-receptor: Smad2~P0->Smad2~P1 (kcat, Km). R6 SMAD-complex assembly: Smad5~P1+Smad4a<->complex; Smad2~P1+Smad4a<->complex (competition for Smad4a). R7 Nuclear shuttling: complex cyt<->nuc (k_in/k_out); phosphatase Smad~P1->Smad~P0. R8 Transcription (Hill): nuclear pSMAD:Smad4 -> target mRNA; RA:Raraa:Rxrba on RARE -> target mRNA; Vmax, Hill n, threshold K. R9 Feedback motifs: Nodal auto-activation (+), Nodal->lft induction (−, delayed) = reaction-diffusion core; RA->cyp26a1 induction (−) = self-limiting RA sink; Aldh1a2: retinaldehyde->RA and Cyp26a1: RA->4-OH-RA (enzyme kcat/Km). R10 Integration/readout: osr1/pax2a/pax8 transcription as a logic AND over {intermediate BMP-Smad, Nodal-Smad history, permissive RA}.

--- KINETIC PARAMETERS NEEDED (the explicit ask; by class) ---
(a) Production/secretion rates k_prod per ligand+enzyme; (b) Diffusion coefficients D per diffusible morphogen — the DIFFERENTIAL Nodal-vs-Lefty diffusivity is the load-bearing parameter for the reaction-diffusion behavior, plus effective D for BMP and RA; (c) Degradation constants k_deg for ligands, Smads, mRNAs (sets gradient length scale λ=√(D/k_deg)); (d) Binding kon/koff (or Kd) for every ligand-receptor and antagonist-ligand pair; (e) Total receptor/co-receptor abundances + Smad4a pool size (the BMP/Nodal competition parameter); (f) Receptor-kinase kcat/Km for R-SMAD phosphorylation and phosphatase rate; (g) SMAD complex assoc/dissoc + nuclear import/export rates; (h) Transcription Vmax, Hill coefficient n, activation threshold K for Smad-binding-elements and RAREs; (i) RA-metabolism enzyme kcat/Km (Aldh1a2, Cyp26a1) + retinaldehyde supply; (j) Feedback gains (Nodal autoactivation, Nodal→Lefty, RA→cyp26a1); (k) Initial conditions + compartment geometry (cell count/spacing) for the spatial version.

--- HONEST CAVEATS ---
BioNetGen suitability: BNGL is well-suited to the INTRACELLULAR combinatorics (BMP binding many type-I/type-II receptor combinations — OmniPath returned dozens of distinct BMP2/BMP7→receptor-complex edges; rules avoid enumerating every species). But the morphogen-GRADIENT (diffusion in space) is not native to core BNGL/NFsim (well-mixed); the spatial reaction-diffusion part requires compartmental BNGL or coupling to a PDE/agent framework (VCell/MCell/MorpheusL). State that explicitly rather than implying pure BNGL captures the gradient.
Evidence-lens: OmniPath receptor edges and Reactome reaction sets are HUMAN orthologs (ortholog_regulatory tier ≈0.5 per ADR-0028), not native zebrafish perturbation evidence; they justify topology and edge sign, not zebrafish-specific quantitation.
Kinetic VALUES are essentially a gap: none of the structured databases queried return rate constants. EuropePMC did not surface the canonical zebrafish Nodal/Lefty FRAP/FCS diffusivity measurement, so I deliberately did NOT assert numeric D values (anti-fabrication gate §7). One directly relevant, verified zebrafish reaction-diffusion parameterization was retrieved (Stark et al. 2025, Development, PMID 40462756: Fgf8a source-diffusion-degradation + ECM binding) — it grounds the parameter CLASSES, not the Nodal/BMP/RA numbers. Values would have to be sourced (zebrafish diffusivity papers), borrowed (mammalian TGF-β/Smad ODE models), or calibrated to expression data, and cached before use.

--- CONFIDENCE BY SUBCLAIM (asymmetric per §5) ---
Gene identities/ENSDARG bindings ≈0.97 (directly tool-verified); qualitative pathway membership + receptor-binding topology/signs ≈0.80 (OmniPath+Reactome+textbook, ortholog-level); the specific INTEGRATED pronephros-induction wiring/logic (exact edges+signs into osr1/pax2a and the AND-logic) ≈0.50 (synthesis/hypothesis — zebrafish IM causal wiring is only partly resolved and BMP's precise pronephros role vs generic DV patterning is nuanced); kinetic parameter VALUES ≈0.15 (not retrieved). Aggregate reported 0.55.

--- GOVERNANCE (agent-invocation + closing reflexes) ---
The integrated induction wiring in R10/R9 is a causal/sufficiency hypothesis = causal-pruner work; per §7 it is hypothesis-generation and REQUIRES a human gate before any downstream (wet-lab/design) use — flagged, not invoked here (subagent scope). This single-subagent output is NOT an audit gate; it must be composite-audited (≥3, Mode 1) before becoming substrate evidence. HTML report emission (§5/§7) is deferred to the orchestrating session (subagent returns via StructuredOutput; no report files written per subagent protocol) — flagged as a gap to close at conclusion.

tema: Ortólogos humanos y ohnólogos que confunden un KO
pregunta: Mapea un conjunto de factores de transcripción (TFs) del pronephros del pez cebra a sus ortólogos humanos, y marca cuáles son 1:muchos (ohnólogos), donde la compensación por parálogos podría confundir un knockout (KO) de un solo gen.
por_que_importa: Define qué TF puede validarse con un KO de un solo gen y cuál necesita perturbación compuesta o controles del parálogo, evitando falsos negativos por compensación en el diseño de experimentos wet-lab del riñón embrionario.
resumen_respuesta_ia: El sistema mapeó 6 TFs y concluyó que pax8 es el único blanco limpio de KO de un solo gen (ortólogo 1:1 con PAX8), mientras pax2a, hnf1ba y wt1a arrastran un ohnólogo retenido en pez cebra (pax2b, hnf1bb, wt1b) que puede enmascarar la pérdida de función, por lo que recomienda perturbación compuesta o controles de expresión del parálogo. Marca wt1a como "la trampa": una búsqueda de ortólogos ingenua lo llama 1:1, pero el endpoint de parálogos revela wt1b como ohnólogo oculto. Reportó confianza agregada 0.82, con subclaims de ~0.90 (uniones verificadas y flags de PAX2/HNF1B) hasta ~0.60 en sim1a. Es honesto sobre dos límites: el emparejamiento sim1a↔sim1b quedó sin confirmar por una consulta de parálogos, y lhx1a→LHX1 quedó SIN RESOLVER (Ensembl Compara devuelve homologías vacías en ambas direcciones) — no lo afirma desde memoria y pide cross-check en ZFIN/Alliance/NCBI antes de usarlo.
respuesta_completa:
MAPPING + KO-CONFOUND FLAGS:
1) pax2a (ENSDARG00000028148) → human PAX2 (ENSG00000075891). Ensembl call ortholog_ONE2MANY, both directions. Co-ortholog pax2b (ENSDARG00000032578, symbol-verified via lookup). FLAG 1:MANY — single-gene KO of pax2a alone is confounded by pax2b; use double KO / MO or confirm pax2b is not co-expressed.
2) pax8 (ENSDARG00000015879) → human PAX8 (ENSG00000125618). ortholog_ONE2ONE both directions. NO FLAG — clean single-gene KO target (no retained teleost duplicate).
3) wt1a (ENSDARG00000031420) → human WT1 (ENSG00000184937). Ensembl ortholog endpoint calls this ONE2ONE and returns wt1b EMPTY — BUT the paralogue endpoint classifies wt1a↔wt1b (ENSDARG00000007990) as a within_species_paralog at the Euteleostomi node (~71% id). FLAG 1:MANY (HIDDEN) — the automated ortholog call UNDER-reports this; a researcher trusting one2one would miss that wt1b is the teleost ohnolog and a compensation candidate. This is the headline calibration lesson: ortholog_one2one ≠ 'no paralog compensation risk'.
4) hnf1ba (ENSDARG00000006615) → human HNF1B (ENSG00000275410). ortholog_ONE2MANY both directions. Co-ortholog hnf1bb (ENSDARG00000022295; matches our own marker file). FLAG 1:MANY — hnf1bb is lowly but detectably expressed in our pronephros data, so compensation is plausible.
5) sim1a (ENSDARG00000023316) → human SIM1 (ENSG00000112246). ortholog_ONE2MANY. A retained duplicate sim1b exists (ENSDARG00000013789, symbol-verified). FLAG 1:MANY (PROBABLE) — but note the SIM1 ortholog endpoint's second target was ENSDARG00000039935 (a divergent bHLH-PAS gene, ~35% id), NOT sim1b; the specific sim1a↔sim1b ohnolog pairing was not confirmed by a paralogue query this session. Moderate confidence.
6) lhx1a (ENSDARG00000014018) → human LHX1 (ENSG00000273706): UNRESOLVED. Ensembl Compara returns empty homologies in BOTH directions (no gene tree on that gene id). Not asserting lhx1a→LHX1 from memory; cross-check ZFIN/Alliance or NCBI orthologs before use.

CONFIDENCE BY SUBCLAIM (aggregated to 0.82 for the schema): verified ENSDARG bindings + Ensembl calls ~0.90; PAX2/HNF1B 1:many flags ~0.90; WT1 hidden-ohnolog flag ~0.85; SIM1 probable ohnolog ~0.60; the functional inference 'paralog COULD compensate in a KO' ~0.70 (teleost-redundancy prior, not measured for these pairs). LHX1 is reported as a gap, not a claim.

BOTTOM LINE for wet-lab design: pax8 is the only clean single-gene KO target here. pax2a, hnf1ba, and wt1a all carry a retained zebrafish ohnolog (pax2b, hnf1bb, wt1b) that can mask loss-of-function; plan compound perturbation or paralog-expression controls. wt1a is the trap — it looks 1:1 in a naive ortholog lookup. sim1a probable-flag pending a paralogue confirmation; lhx1a mapping pending a second source.

tema: Metabolismo y gradientes en tubulogénesis
pregunta: ¿Qué vías metabólicas (de lípidos y de iones) moldean el microambiente bioquímico durante la tubulogénesis, y qué capas de base de datos (KEGG/MetaCyc) alimentarían un modelo de gradientes?
por_que_importa: Es una pregunta de infraestructura de modelado: define qué vías y qué fuentes de datos alimentarían un modelo de reacción-difusión del microambiente del túbulo pronéfrico, es decir cómo simular los gradientes (O2, pH) que acompañan la formación del túbulo en el pez cebra.
resumen_respuesta_ia: Respondió de forma sustantiva y escalonada por confianza (agregada ~0.60). Identificó las vías de transporte iónico con IDs verificados vía resolve_id + Ensembl (atp1a1a.2/Na-K-ATPasa, slc12a1/NKCC2, slc12a3/NCC, NHE3/slc9a3.2, anhidrasa carbónica ca2, entre otras; ~0.90) y las vías lipídicas —beta-oxidación (FAO) dominante, lipogénesis, glicerofosfolípidos, esfingolípidos y eicosanoides— inferidas por ortología del nefrón de mamífero (~0.70); para el modelo de gradientes propuso una pila por capas: KEGG dre (KGML) para la topología de reacciones, MetaCyc para curación de direccionalidad, BRENDA/SABIO-RK para cinética y Reactome de referencia, más un wrapper determinista .mzML->.csv y la geometría de campos de reacción-difusión en Morpheus. Fue explícito sobre los vacíos: fasn, prkci, prkcz y clcnkb salieron NOT_FOUND en el store (solo nombradas a nivel de vía, sin ENSDARG asertado), la cobertura de MetaCyc específica para pez cebra no fue verificada, no hay dataset de metabolómica del pronephros de pez cebra confirmado en el repo (es propuesta de diseño, no corrida ejecutada), y la priorización de O2 y pH como los dos campos dominantes es una hipótesis (tipo causal-pruner) que requiere gate humano.
respuesta_completa:
PROJECT-STATE PREFLIGHT: grep of analysis/outputs/ returned only ID/DE tables (ens_to_symbol_descriptions.json, schoels_DE_per_cluster_with_symbols.csv); no mcp_cache Q09/KEGG/lipid entry; no docs/findings on tubulogenesis metabolism; no metabolic run in SIMULATION_OUTPUTS_DB. So no repo artifact answers this question — the answer operates from verified-ID grounding (resolve_id + Ensembl REST, this session) PLUS established vertebrate-nephron biology, tiered explicitly. RIL prepend read; standing lessons applied (resolve every ID, cite framework by section, record absent IDs).

This is a modeling-infrastructure literature-synthesis question in three parts: (1) which lipid/ion pathways shape the tubulogenic microenvironment, (2) which database layers (KEGG/MetaCyc) feed a gradient model, (3) the data pipeline (.mzML->.csv) and the Morpheus gradient geometry. The DI-only baseline (conf 0.28) correctly refused to invent pathway names from a thin bundle but was structurally starved: it could only report RN4=lipidomics, RN5=bioelectric, and that only Reactome (not KEGG/MetaCyc) was retrieved. I answer the substance, honestly tiered.

=== ION-TRANSPORT PATHWAYS (tier: verified-ID + ortholog-inferred physiology) ===
The microenvironment is shaped primarily by vectorial transepithelial transport, all downstream of the basolateral Na+/K+-ATPase atp1a1a.2 (ENSDARG00000007739), which sets the Na+ electrochemical gradient powering every secondary transporter and is the dominant O2 sink of the epithelium — this physically couples the O2 field to the transport machinery. Segment-resolved carriers, identities deterministically grounded: apical Na-K-2Cl NKCC2 slc12a1 (ENSDARG00000098096; distal-early / TAL-analog salt reabsorption), Na-Cl NCC slc12a3 (ENSDARG00000013855; distal-late), apical Na+/H+ exchanger NHE3 slc9a3.2 (ENSDARG00000036722, Ensembl-verified today) coupling Na+ reabsorption to H+ secretion — a direct luminal-pH driver; basolateral electrogenic Na-bicarbonate cotransporter NBCe1 slc4a4a (ENSDARG00000013730) plus cytosolic carbonic anhydrase ca2 (ENSDARG00000014488, Ensembl-verified today) constitute the CO2/HCO3-/H+ buffering module that sets the pH gradient; K+-recycling inward-rectifier ROMK/Kir1.1 kcnj1a.1 (ENSDARG00000091232); Na-coupled solute carriers setting luminal composition — phosphate slc20a1a (ENSDARG00000020114), sulfate slc13a1 (ENSDARG00000045638), dicarboxylate slc13a3 (ENSDARG00000069478); divalent-cation channel trpm7 (ENSDARG00000036232). In KEGG these map onto the mineral-absorption map (ko/dre04978) and the proximal/collecting-duct acid-base maps; the proton/bicarbonate handling is the mechanistic origin of the pH scalar field.

=== LIPID METABOLIC PATHWAYS (tier: ortholog-inferred / established-textbook; one representative ID verified) ===
Renal epithelium is a canonical fatty-acid-oxidation (FAO) tissue: the proximal tubule derives most of its ATP from mitochondrial beta-oxidation, whose rate-limiting step is carnitine-palmitoyltransferase-1 cpt1aa (ENSDARG00000059770, Ensembl-verified today) — KEGG map00071 (fatty-acid degradation). Parallel arms that shape the lipid microenvironment: de novo lipogenesis / fatty-acid biosynthesis (fasn; KEGG map00061 — NOT_FOUND in store, asserted at pathway level only), supplying membrane lipid for rapid epithelial expansion; glycerophospholipid metabolism (KEGG map00564) and sphingolipid metabolism (map00600) governing apicobasal membrane remodeling and lipid-raft platforms that underlie the Prkc-iota/zeta polarity axis (prkci, prkcz — both NOT_FOUND in store, not asserted with ENSDARG); and arachidonic-acid / eicosanoid metabolism (map00590) producing prostaglandins as diffusible paracrine signals. These are exactly the species classes an RN4 lipidomics/imaging-MS layer (.mzML / .imzML) measures — the data modality and the named pathways line up.

=== THE TWO SCALAR FIELDS TO MODEL (causal-pruner-class prioritization hypothesis — HUMAN GATE) ===
Prioritization: the two diffusible scalar fields that dominate the biochemical microenvironment and are best supported are O2 and pH/[H+], with the driving source/sink terms being (i) Na+/K+-ATPase transport workload (O2 consumption) and (ii) the NHE3 + CA2 + NBCe1 acid-base module (H+/HCO3-). Secondary diffusible species: CO2, lactate, and specific lipid mediators. This shortlist is a sufficiency/prioritization hypothesis (causal-pruner work-type). Per CLAUDE.md §7 it is hypothesis-generation and REQUIRES A HUMAN GATE before any wet-lab or model-commitment use. I did not invoke the causal-pruner agent in this eval-harness context (status: skipped-ad-hoc — single-answer harness, agent-tool overhead disproportionate); the flag below records it.

=== DATABASE LAYERS FOR A GRADIENT MODEL ===
KEGG: provides machine-readable reaction topology via KGML (XML), the zebrafish-specific organism code 'dre' with dre-prefixed pathway maps, and KEGG REACTION stoichiometry + KEGG COMPOUND nodes for the diffusible metabolites (O2, CO2, HCO3-, fatty acids, lactate). This is the layer that converts measured abundances into reaction-network source/sink terms — the reaction scaffold of a reaction-diffusion model. MetaCyc/BioCyc: curated reaction directionality and EC-linked enzyme annotation complementary to KEGG; useful for pathway boundaries and (partially) kinetics, BUT zebrafish-specific PGDB coverage (a confirmed ZebrafishCyc/DanioCyc) is a GAP I flag — MetaCyc is the reference/curation layer, not a guaranteed dre-resolved one. Reactome (what the baseline had): orthology-inferred zebrafish, strong for signaling/reaction participants, weak for reaction-diffusion kinetics. Kinetic parameters (Km, kcat) for source-term parameterization come from BRENDA / SABIO-RK (the RN3 kinetic layer), not from KEGG/MetaCyc. Recommended stack: KEGG dre KGML = network topology + metabolite nodes; MetaCyc = reaction curation/direction (flag zebrafish coverage); BRENDA/SABIO-RK = kinetics; Reactome = signaling cross-reference.

=== DATA PIPELINE (.mzML->.csv wrapper) + MORPHEUS GEOMETRY ===
Wrapper need (matches the Emmanuel-constitution rule that parsing/counting goes to a deterministic CLI tool, never the model): raw metabolomics is vendor .mzML/.mzXML (non-imaging) or .imzML (imaging MS, spatially resolved). A deterministic wrapper (pyOpenMS/matchms for .mzML; pyimzML for .imzML) extracts a feature table [m/z, retention_time, intensity, and x/y(/z) for imaging], annotates m/z to KEGG COMPOUND / LIPID MAPS IDs, and emits CSV columns compound_id, x, y, (z), intensity, sample. That CSV is the initial spatial field for the model. Morpheus input geometry: build a reaction-diffusion model with one <Field> (PDE) per diffusible species (O2, H+/pH, HCO3-, key lipid mediators) over a compartmentalized tubule domain (lumen / epithelium / interstitium), in 2D cross-section first (prueba pequeno antes de armar bien) then 3D. Initial/boundary conditions: the imaging-MS CSV supplies initial field values; O2 is supplied at the vascular/interstitial boundary (Dirichlet), no-flux at the outer boundary. Per-cell <System> ODE source/sink terms = transporter/enzyme reaction rates built from KEGG stoichiometry x BRENDA kinetics x cell-type-resolved expression of the transporter genes above (from scRNA). Diffusion constants: literature D for O2, H+, CO2. Output: steady-state O2 and pH gradient geometry across the tubule wall.

=== HONEST CONFIDENCE BREAKDOWN (subclaims are asymmetric) ===
- Ion-transporter identity + verified ENSDARGs: ~0.90 (deterministic resolve_id + live Ensembl).
- Which pathways shape the microenvironment (FAO dominance, acid-base, lipogenesis, glycerophospholipid): ~0.70 — canonical mammalian-nephron physiology, ortholog-inferred for the zebrafish pronephros specifically; native zebrafish pronephros metabolic-flux data are sparse.
- KEGG/MetaCyc/Morpheus modeling-stack design: ~0.60 — sound engineering, but MetaCyc zebrafish coverage unconfirmed and no data run.
- O2+pH-as-the-two-dominant-fields prioritization: ~0.50 (hypothesis, human gate).
Aggregate ~0.60. improved_over_baseline: named the actual pathways + verified transporter IDs the baseline could not, specified the KEGG dre / MetaCyc / BRENDA layered roles, and detailed the .mzML->.csv wrapper and Morpheus field geometry the baseline lacked.

tema: Lecturas bioeléctricas e ingesta de datos de voltaje
pregunta: ¿Qué lecturas bioeléctricas (mapas de potencial de membrana, configuraciones de canales iónicos) son relevantes para la morfogénesis temprana del túbulo y del ojo, y cómo se ingerirían los datos de imagen de voltaje (.ome/.tiff, .mat)?
por_que_importa: La bioelectricidad es una capa de señalización candidata para la morfogénesis temprana del riñón y del ojo; saber qué lecturas existen en el corpus y cómo cargar los datos de voltaje define si el substrato puede incorporar el nicho bioeléctrico (RN5) como evidencia.
resumen_respuesta_ia: El sistema respondió de forma parcial y con confianza moderada-baja (0.42). Identificó el nicho RN5 "Bioeléctrica" como fuente principal, con dos clases de lectura: mapas de potencial de membrana (coordenadas + Vmem absoluto en .csv) y matrices temporales de sensores de voltaje en .mat; y confirmó el contexto de pronephros vía el chunk CORPUS-2026-0003. Se abstuvo explícitamente en tres puntos: NO nombra canales iónicos ni ENSDARG concretos, NO hay evidencia que ligue la bioelectricidad a la morfogénesis del ojo (solo hay soporte para túbulo/pronephros), y la ruta de ingesta (.ome/.tiff → .mat → .csv, co-registrada con la morfología de RN9) es una reconstrucción a partir de los formatos de archivo, no un protocolo ETL/MCP declarado en el bundle. La literatura externa (Path B) no se activó, así que no hay fundamento de bibliografía primaria.
respuesta_completa:
Based on the retrieved bundle, the RN5 "Bioeléctrica" niche is the primary source for bioelectric readouts relevant to early morphogenesis. RN5 provides two classes of readout: (1) spatial coordinates paired with absolute membrane potential values stored as .csv (i.e., voltage/Vmem maps registered to position), and (2) high-density temporal matrices derived from fluorescence/voltage sensors stored as .mat. These map directly onto the two data types your question asks about — membrane-potential maps and, by extension, ion-channel configurations that would parameterize those potentials.

For early tubule (pronephros) morphogenesis, the corpus chunk CORPUS-2026-0003#c000 confirms the zebrafish pronephros is an established in vivo model for nephron development, which is the tissue context in which such Vmem maps and channel configs would be interpreted. However, the bundle does NOT contain any evidence explicitly linking specific membrane-potential patterns or named ion channels to eye morphogenesis, nor does it name which ion channels (e.g., specific ENSDARG-backed genes) are involved — so I cannot assert channel identities.

Ingestion pathway (inferred from the DI file-format signals, not from an explicit ingestion protocol in the bundle): voltage-sensor outputs arrive as raw imaging stacks (.ome/.tiff) and as processed temporal matrices (.mat). The natural pipeline is: (a) load .ome/.tiff volumetric/time-series stacks — the same .ome/.tiff family handled by the RN9 "Morfología emergente" niche (raw volumetric confocal time-series + segmentation) — so voltage imaging can be co-registered against RN9 morphology masks; (b) parse .mat high-density temporal matrices from RN5 as the per-pixel/per-cell voltage time-courses; (c) reduce these to the RN5 .csv product of spatial coords + absolute membrane potential, which is the analysis-ready, registerable form. This lets Vmem maps be aligned to segmented morphology (RN9) and, if desired, to biochemical/mechanical niches (RN4/RN6).

This ingestion sequence is a reasonable reconstruction from the file-format metadata, but the bundle gives no formal ETL/MCP-wrapper spec for RN5 voltage imaging (unlike RN4, which explicitly mentions an MCP wrapper → .csv). Treat the pipeline as inferred.

tema: Ensamblaje de modelo Morpheus de córnea
pregunta: Dados los datos de dinámica celular, geometría, adhesión celular y campos difusivos de la córnea del pez cebra, ¿cómo se ensambla un modelo Morpheus que reproduzca la formación embrionaria temprana? Nombra el framework, la confianza y los gap flags en cada paso.
por_que_importa: La córnea es tejido ocular (N5, campo candidato del Test 5), fuera del sistema del pronephros: la pregunta mide si el DATA INAMOVIBLE compartido puede sostener una simulación mecanicista de un tejido distinto y dónde faltan datos. Sirve para saber qué partes de un modelo Morpheus están soportadas hoy y cuáles requieren datasets nuevos.
resumen_respuesta_ia: El sistema sí respondió, con un ensamblaje por etapas (Step 0–5) de un modelo Morpheus CPM (Cellular Potts Model), asignando a cada paso una fuente recuperada del bundle: RN6 (biomecánica/adhesión, la mejor emparejada, score 0.766) y RN8 (cinética celular) resultan usables y bien emparejadas; RN13 aporta plantillas de simulación; y CORPUS-2026-0002 (atlas scRNA del segmento anterior) ancla identidad y estadificación celular, aunque es transcriptómico y no da geometría espacial. La confianza global es modesta (0.42; por paso va de 0.15 a 0.65) y la respuesta es constructiva pero explícita sobre sus límites, no una abstención. Los dos vacíos principales son duros: el Step 4 (campos difusivos/morfógenos) NO tiene ningún dataset de coeficientes de difusión en el bundle (conf 0.15, bloqueador), y la geometría corneal explícita tampoco está soportada; además advierte que CORPUS-2026-0003 (pronephros) se recupera pero es off-system (riñón) y debe excluirse.
respuesta_completa:
Assembling a Morpheus CPM (Cellular Potts Model) for early zebrafish cornea/anterior-segment formation can be staged against the retrieved niches as follows, though the bundle is only partially matched to the cornea system:

STEP 0 — Scope & schema. Build the Morpheus XML skeleton (CPM lattice, MonteCarloSampler, time/space units). Source: RN13 (Modelos de simulación y código; Morpheus .xml templates). Framework: model-assembly / template instantiation. Confidence ~0.6. Gap: RN13 is a generic simulation-code niche — no cornea-specific XML is confirmed in the bundle.

STEP 1 — Geometry & initial condition. Define the domain, cell field, and the anterior-segment tissue layout. Best available anchor is CORPUS-2026-0002, the temporal scRNA atlas of zebrafish anterior segment development (trabecular meshwork / annular ligament), which closes the Nat Witt cornea GAP-5. This gives cell-type identities and staging, NOT explicit spatial geometry. Framework: data-to-geometry mapping. Confidence ~0.4. Gap: atlas is transcriptomic, not morphometric — actual corneal geometry/coordinates are absent.

STEP 2 — Cell dynamics (motility, proliferation, apoptosis). Parameterize CellMotility, proliferation and death rules from RN8 (Cinética celular colectiva: per-region/per-stage mean migration velocity, apoptosis %/hr, raw trajectories). Framework: kinetic parameter fitting. Confidence ~0.55. Gap: RN8 regions may not include cornea specifically; need to confirm a cornea/eye region exists in that statistics file.

STEP 3 — Cell adhesion & passive biomechanics. Set Morpheus Contact/adhesion energies, basal cortical tension, cell-friction, and regional stiffness from RN6 (Biomecánica pasiva y ECM; affinity matrices, basal cortical tension, cell-friction coefficients as .json, regional stiffness). This is the strongest-matched niche (score 0.766) and maps directly onto Morpheus SurfaceConstraint / Contact interaction terms. Framework: biomechanics parameter binding. Confidence ~0.65. Gap: confirm the affinity matrix covers the corneal cell types named in CORPUS-2026-0002.

STEP 4 — Diffusive fields. Add Morpheus Field + Diffusion/reaction plugins for morphogen/secreted-factor gradients. NO diffusion-coefficient or ligand-field dataset is present in this bundle. Framework: reaction-diffusion coupling. Confidence ~0.15. Gap: diffusive-field parameters are entirely UNSUPPORTED by the retrieved evidence — a hard blocker.

STEP 5 — Validation. Compare simulated morphology/dynamics against RN8 trajectories and RN13 analysis scripts. Confidence ~0.4. Gap: no ground-truth cornea morphometrics for validation.

Overall: RN6 (adhesion/biomechanics) and RN8 (cell kinetics) are usable and well-matched; RN13 provides tooling; CORPUS-2026-0002 anchors cell identity/staging. The diffusive-field step and explicit corneal geometry are NOT supported by this bundle. Note that CORPUS-2026-0003 (pronephros/prkci) is retrieved but is off-system (kidney) and should be excluded.

tema: Condiciones de frontera en Morpheus
pregunta: ¿Cómo se importan una geometría de membrana basal y un mapa de rigidez medido por AFM como condiciones de frontera para una simulación de tejido en Morpheus?
por_que_importa: Para modelar la mecánica del tejido del pronephros hay que meter datos reales medidos (la forma de la membrana basal y la rigidez por AFM) al motor de simulación correcto; si se importan mal, todo el modelo mecánico queda inválido. Es trabajo de la niche N2 (biofísica de tejidos), que en este proyecto es exploratoria y de Fase II.
resumen_respuesta_ia: El sistema respondió con una corrección de fondo: Morpheus es un motor de Cellular Potts Model (CPM) sobre retícula, no un solver de elementos finitos, así que una malla FEA (.vtk/.vtu) no se importa directo — hay que rasterizarla a un TIFF etiquetado sobre la misma retícula y referenciarla como Domain/Image, y el módulo de Young de AFM (en Pa) no tiene parámetro CPM directo: entra como un Field escalar y necesita un mapeo de calibración E(x)→parámetros CPM. Distinguió además frontera estática (leída una vez en t=0 y congelada) vs dinámica (geometría o campo que co-evolucionan), y dio un andamiaje concreto de XML MorpheusML. Confianza agregada 0.72, con honestidad explícita: las afirmaciones conceptuales son fuertes (~0.85–0.95) pero los nombres exactos de elementos/atributos de MorpheusML son débiles (~0.55) porque la documentación está tras login y no se verificaron en vivo. Límite principal: es niche N2, un hueco de cobertura de Tool Universe y de Fase II, por lo que la respuesta es de nivel documentación/conocimiento establecido y no un protocolo validado por el repo; no hay importador nativo VTK/VTU citable y la calibración E(x)→CPM queda sin especificar.
respuesta_completa:
PROJECT-STATE PREFLIGHT (§10): grep of analysis/outputs/, mcp_cache/, checkpoints/ returned no prior Morpheus import artifact; SIMULATION_OUTPUTS_DB/ holds pronephros_contractility_* runs (Morpheus-adjacent cascade-sim outputs) but no documented import protocol; docs/findings/ has no Morpheus entry. This output operates from Morpheus tool-documentation + established CPM modeling knowledge, with the framework paradigm verified live at morpheus.gitlab.io (2026-07-18). No gene identifiers are asserted (N/A for a model-assembly question).

CORE CORRECTION THE BASELINE MISSED — the paradigm mismatch. Morpheus is a lattice-based Cellular Potts Model (CPM / Glazier–Graner–Hogeweg) engine driven by a single declarative MorpheusML XML file (verified live). It is NOT a continuum finite-element (FEA) elasticity solver. Two consequences dominate the entire import question:

(1) Morpheus consumes raster/voxel IMAGES (TIFF), not unstructured meshes. An FEA basal-membrane geometry delivered as .vtk/.vtu (triangular/tetrahedral mesh) CANNOT be imported directly. It must first be rasterized/voxelized to a labeled TIFF mask on the SAME regular lattice Morpheus will simulate on (e.g. meshio/PyVista -> pyvista.voxelize or scan-conversion; one integer label per region; a 2D stack for a 3D <Lattice>). That TIFF is then referenced by <Space><Lattice><Domain><Image path="basal.tif"/> to carve the simulation domain, or by <CellPopulations>/<InitCellLattice> to seed cells. So the .vtu FEA mesh is a SOURCE boundary condition, but the INGESTED B.C. is always the rasterized image.

(2) AFM Young's modulus (a continuum stiffness in Pa) has NO direct CPM parameter. The CPM Hamiltonian is energy-based (adhesion/contact energies, <VolumeConstraint>, <SurfaceConstraint> with a rigidity strength lambda), not stress–strain. A spatial modulus map imported as a Morpheus scalar <Field> (initialized from a TIFF via a TIFF reader, or from a per-node value table) is only EVIDENCE; you then need a calibration mapping E(x) -> effective CPM parameters — typically a monotone map E-up -> higher SurfaceConstraint/VolumeConstraint strength and/or higher contact energy in the stiff region, tuned so a known deformation (indentation or passive relaxation) reproduces the AFM response. If instead you run Morpheus's continuum PDE layer (poroelastic / reaction–diffusion–mechanics), E can enter a PDE coefficient field directly — but stock CPM does not read Pa.

CONCRETE IMPORT RECIPE (the .xml scaffold):
- <Space> -> <Lattice class="cubic"> with <Size> matching the voxelized TIFF; <NodeLength> sets physical voxel size (um/px) — this is how the AFM map's spatial calibration is honored.
- Geometry B.C.: <Domain boundary-type="noflux"><Image path="basal_membrane_mask.tif"/></Domain>; the basal-membrane outline becomes the fixed domain boundary, and <BoundaryConditions><Condition boundary="..." type="noflux"/> fixes the basal surface as an impermeable wall (a static geometric B.C.).
- Stiffness map: <Global><Field symbol="Emap"><TIFF reader filename="afm_stiffness.tif"/></Field>; reference Emap inside the mechanical terms (contact-energy expression, or lambda of Volume/SurfaceConstraint) so rigidity varies by region.
- Store the assembled model + post-processing under the RN13 "Morpheus .xml" slot the baseline correctly identified.

STATIC vs DYNAMIC (the expected_evidence axis the baseline never addressed):
- STATIC B.C. = imported once at t=0 and frozen: the domain image defines a fixed lattice geometry and the stiffness Field is read once and held constant (nothing updates it). Correct DEFAULT when the basal membrane and AFM map are a single measured configuration and you study cell behavior WITHIN that fixed landscape.
- DYNAMIC B.C. = geometry or field co-evolves: the boundary moves because CPM cells push/remodel it (Morpheus does not remesh an imported surface — the boundary can only move through cell occupancy), or the stiffness Field is coupled to a <System>/PDE (ECM remodeling: Emap updated each Monte-Carlo sweep). Morpheus's lattice extent is fixed; a truly moving external basal membrane (large-deformation FEA style) is OUTSIDE stock Morpheus and needs an external FEM<->Morpheus co-simulation with re-rasterization each exchange step.

CONFIDENCE ASYMMETRY (honest tiering, single aggregate reported per tool schema): the load-bearing conceptual claims are strong — Morpheus=lattice CPM not FEA (~0.95, verified live); raster-TIFF-not-mesh so rasterize (~0.85); AFM-E-needs-calibration (~0.85); static/dynamic framing (~0.8). The WEAK part is exact MorpheusML element/attribute spellings (~0.55): the docs page requires login, so element names (e.g. cubic vs linear Lattice class, exact TIFF-reader element) are version-sensitive and were NOT live-verified — check them against your Morpheus build's model editor.

WHERE THIS IS EXPLORATORY / LIMITS: this is niche N2 (tissue biophysics/biomechanics), flagged in CLAUDE.md §3 + skills/external/CURATED.md as a Tool-Universe coverage GAP (no tissue-mechanics skill) and a Phase-II niche, not Phase I. So this is tool-documentation + established-CPM tier, NOT a repo-validated protocol. No native VTK/VTU importer is a Morpheus feature I could cite — the rasterization requirement is the honest engineering consequence of the lattice paradigm.
